NOT_AS_DESCRIBED.summary: Almost all of these returns are wired headphones and earbuds. The biggest complaint is fit and comfort: they are too small or too big (especially for children), hurt the ears, or fall out. Next come sound that is tinny or has weak bass, the 'midnight blue' color arriving purple, connectors that don't match the buyer's phone or device, and 'noise cancelling' claims the product doesn't live up to. Only about 3-4% of comments are empty filler like 'Not as Expected' or 'No'.

DEFECTIVE.summary: Defective returns are dominated by wired earphones/headphones that produce no sound at all, play in only one ear, or sound distorted, staticky or muffled, often right out of the box or after a few days to weeks of use. Broken in-line volume/play controls and non-working microphones (callers can't hear the customer) are the other big functional complaints, with smaller groups citing intermittent connections, poor fit/comfort, or compatibility problems mislabeled as defects. Around 4-5% of comments are empty or generic (e.g. just "Defective", "Not working", "Na").

themes.detail: Earphones produce no audio at all when plugged in, often across multiple devices, or stop working entirely after hours to a few weeks.

NOT_COMPATIBLE.summary: Most compatibility returns come down to the wrong plug: customers needed USB-C or Lightning (especially for newer iPhones and iPads) or a different jack size, and the wired product did not fit their port. Others report the headphones not working with specific devices (laptops, Chromebooks, school computers, pianos, game consoles), expected Bluetooth/wireless, or use the code for physical fit, missing or non-working mic, volume control and sound quality issues. Roughly 10% of comments are empty or one-word (e.g. "Not Compatible", "Yes", "Phone", "Port").

UNWANTED_ITEM.summary: Most of these returns are simple changes of mind. Nearly half use only the stock 'My needs changed' option or say 'no longer needed', and about one in six found or kept another product. The free-text comments that do explain more mention unwanted gifts, wanting wireless/Bluetooth or a different plug or feature, fit and comfort, accidental duplicate orders and late delivery. Roughly 4% are placeholder text such as 'Na', 'N' or 'J'.
